title: Universal Male Suffrage Established
description: Following the 'Revolution of 1933', young Andorran men demanded political reform and universal male suffrage was granted, replacing a system in which only heads of household could vote. French gendarmes were briefly deployed to the principality to restore order during the unrest.

title: Boris Skossyreff Proclaims Himself King of Andorra
description: Russian-born adventurer Boris Skossyreff issued a proclamation in Urgell declaring himself 'Boris I, King of Andorra', then promptly declared war on the Bishop of Urgell. He was arrested by Spanish authorities within days, but the bizarre episode underscored the fragility of the principality's micro-state institutions.

title: Spanish Civil War Spillover Concerns
description: The outbreak of the Spanish Civil War threatened Andorra's southern border and the principality hosted refugees fleeing the conflict. The Bishop of Urgell co-prince's authority was complicated by the war engulfing his diocese in Catalonia.

title: Andorra Declares Neutrality in WWII
description: At the outbreak of World War II, Andorra formally declared its neutrality, a policy it would maintain throughout the conflict despite being wedged between Vichy France and Franco's Spain. The principality became an important smuggling and escape route for refugees, downed Allied airmen, and Jews fleeing Nazi-occupied Europe.

title: Pyrenean Smuggling Route for Refugees
description: Andorran 'passadors' (people-smugglers) operated extensively across the Pyrenees, helping thousands of refugees, Jews, and Allied servicemen escape Nazi-occupied France into Spain via the principality. The wartime smuggling economy reshaped Andorran society and laid foundations for postwar contraband trade.

title: Andorra Formally Ends State of War with Germany
description: Andorra signed a treaty officially ending its state of war with Germany, having been technically still 'at war' since 1914 due to its omission from the Treaty of Versailles. The diplomatic anomaly was finally resolved 13 years after WWII ended, illustrating Andorra's marginal position in the European state system.

title: Postwar Tourism and Retail Boom Begins
description: Andorra's status as a duty-free enclave between France and Spain drove a major expansion of cross-border shopping tourism in the 1960s, with consumer goods, alcohol, tobacco and electronics drawing millions of day-trippers. The economy began its decisive shift away from subsistence agriculture toward services.

title: Pas de la Casa Ski Resort Expansion
description: Major expansion of the Pas de la Casa ski station near the French border accelerated Andorra's transformation into a Pyrenean winter sports destination. Ski tourism would become a second economic pillar alongside duty-free retail.

title: Female Suffrage Granted
description: Andorran women were granted the right to vote in 1970, with the right to stand for elected office following in 1973. Andorra was among the last European jurisdictions to enfranchise women, though enfranchised native-born women still excluded the majority of foreign-born residents.

title: First Executive Council Established
description: Constitutional reforms created an Executive Council (Govern) headed by a Cap de Govern (Head of Government), introducing for the first time a separation between legislative (General Council) and executive functions. Òscar Ribas Reig became the first Cap de Govern.

title: Òscar Ribas Reig First Head of Government
description: Òscar Ribas Reig was sworn in as Andorra's first Cap de Govern under the new institutional arrangement, beginning the gradual modernisation of the principality's medieval governance structures. He would later steer Andorra toward its 1993 Constitution.

title: EU Customs Union Agreement
description: Andorra signed a customs union agreement with the European Economic Community covering industrial goods, ending the principality's full duty-free status for non-agricultural products. The deal was a precursor to deeper European engagement and forced gradual harmonisation of trade rules.

title: Modern Constitution Adopted by Referendum
description: Andorrans approved a new democratic constitution by referendum on 14 March 1993 with 74% in favour, formally transforming the principality into a parliamentary democracy with the Bishop of Urgell and the President of France as ceremonial co-princes. The constitution ended 715 years of feudal arrangements dating to the 1278 Pareatges.

title: Andorra Admitted to United Nations
description: Andorra became the 184th member state of the United Nations on 28 July 1993, marking its emergence as a fully sovereign actor in the international system after centuries as a semi-feudal co-principality. UN membership followed swiftly on the heels of constitutional reform.

title: Andorra Joins Council of Europe
description: Andorra acceded to the Council of Europe in November 1994, formally committing to European human rights standards and the European Convention on Human Rights. Membership reinforced the post-1993 constitutional turn toward liberal democratic norms.

title: First Elections Under New Constitution
description: The first parliamentary elections under the 1993 Constitution were held in December 1993, with Òscar Ribas Reig's Liberal Party (later Liberal Union) winning a plurality. The vote inaugurated competitive multi-party democracy in the principality.

title: Marc Forné Molné Becomes Head of Government
description: Liberal Union leader Marc Forné Molné became Cap de Govern after the 1997 elections, beginning a long centre-right tenure that would oversee Andorra's gradual integration with European financial regulatory norms.

title: Euro Adopted as De Facto Currency
description: Although not an EU or eurozone member, Andorra adopted the euro as its de facto currency from 2002 following the retirement of the French franc and Spanish peseta. The principality lacked a formal monetary agreement until 2011 and could not initially mint its own coins.

title: OECD Greylist for Tax Haven Status
description: Andorra was placed on the OECD 'grey list' of uncooperative tax jurisdictions in April 2009, alongside Liechtenstein and Monaco, prompting urgent reform commitments. Co-Prince Nicolas Sarkozy publicly threatened to resign as co-prince if Andorra did not abandon its tax haven model.

title: Bank Secrecy Reform Commitments
description: Under intense international pressure, Andorra signed Tax Information Exchange Agreements (TIEAs) with multiple OECD members and committed to dismantling its strict bank secrecy regime. The reforms ended a defining pillar of Andorra's century-old offshore financial model.

title: EU Monetary Agreement Signed
description: Andorra signed a monetary agreement with the European Union in June 2011 formalising its use of the euro and granting permission to mint its own euro coins from 2014. The deal also bound Andorra to adopt EU banking, anti-money-laundering, and counter-terrorism financing legislation.

title: Personal Income Tax Introduced
description: Andorra introduced a non-resident income tax in 2011 followed by a general personal income tax (IRPF) in 2015, dismantling its historic status as a no-income-tax jurisdiction. The reforms were driven by OECD pressure, the EU monetary agreement, and the need to diversify state revenue.

title: Banking Transparency Reforms Completed
description: Andorra signed the OECD Multilateral Convention on Mutual Administrative Assistance in Tax Matters and committed to automatic exchange of financial information from 2018. The principality was removed from key tax haven blacklists, completing its transition to a transparent financial centre.

title: Banca Privada d'Andorra US Treasury Sanctions
description: On 10 March 2015 the US Treasury's FinCEN designated Banca Privada d'Andorra (BPA) as a primary money laundering concern under section 311 of the USA PATRIOT Act, alleging the bank facilitated laundering for Russian, Chinese, and Venezuelan organised crime. The designation triggered the bank's collapse and a sovereign reputational crisis.

title: BPA Bank Resolution and Vall Banc Creation
description: Andorran authorities placed BPA into resolution, separating clean deposits into a new bank, Vall Banc, which was sold to US private equity firm JC Flowers in 2016. The episode prompted comprehensive overhaul of Andorran banking supervision and AML institutions (AFA, UIFAND).

title: BPA Criminal Investigation and Trials Begin
description: Criminal investigations and trials against BPA executives, Andorran officials, and clients accelerated in 2017, becoming one of the largest political-financial scandals in the principality's history. The fallout damaged trust in the financial sector and accelerated regulatory reform.

title: Xavier Espot Zamora Becomes Head of Government
description: Xavier Espot Zamora of Democrats for Andorra (DA) became Cap de Govern after the April 2019 elections, succeeding Antoni Martí. His government inherited the post-BPA reform agenda and accelerated EU association negotiations.

title: Early COVID-19 Lockdown Imposed
description: Andorra closed its borders, ski resorts, and non-essential businesses on 14 March 2020 in response to the COVID-19 pandemic, one of the earliest comprehensive shutdowns in Europe. The closure of ski tourism in mid-season caused severe economic disruption to the principality's main winter industry.

title: Whole-Population COVID Antibody Testing
description: Andorra became one of the first countries to attempt mass antibody testing of its entire population, conducting two rounds of testing in May-June 2020. The micro-state's small population enabled comprehensive epidemiological surveillance unfeasible in larger jurisdictions.

title: Tourism-Driven Recession
description: Andorra's GDP contracted sharply in 2020 as ski tourism, retail tourism, and cross-border shopping collapsed under pandemic restrictions. The principality recorded its worst economic downturn since records began, exposing the fragility of an undiversified service economy.

title: COVID Recovery and Vaccination Rollout
description: Andorra received vaccine supplies via bilateral arrangements with Spain and France, beginning vaccination in February 2021. Tourism gradually reopened through 2021 and the economy began a slow recovery.

title: Corporate Tax Rate Aligned with EU Norms
description: Andorra continued harmonising its corporate tax framework with EU and OECD standards, including BEPS implementation and minimum substance requirements. The reforms positioned Andorra as a low-tax but compliant jurisdiction rather than an offshore haven.

title: Espot Re-elected for Second Term
description: Democrats for Andorra under Xavier Espot won the April 2023 parliamentary elections, securing a second term for the Cap de Govern with a coalition including Liberals of Andorra. The campaign was dominated by housing affordability, immigration, and the EU association agreement.

title: EU Association Agreement Negotiations Concluded
description: Andorra, alongside San Marino, concluded negotiations on a comprehensive EU association agreement in December 2023 covering free movement of goods, services, capital, and persons. The deal would deeply integrate the principality into the EU single market while preserving formal sovereignty.

title: Joves d'Andorra Anti-Immigration Protests
description: The 'Joves d'Andorra' (Youth of Andorra) movement organised protests in 2024 against high levels of immigration and rising housing costs that they argued were displacing native Andorrans, who form less than half of the principality's population. The protests highlighted growing tensions over demographic change in the micro-state.

title: Housing Affordability Crisis
description: Andorran rents and house prices surged sharply in 2023-2024 driven by foreign investment, digital nomad inflows, and constrained land supply, prompting government emergency measures including a moratorium on foreign property purchases for non-residents. Housing became the dominant domestic political issue.

title: EU Association Agreement Signed
description: Andorra signed the EU Association Agreement in 2025, with ratification proceeding through national parliaments and the European Parliament. The agreement marks the deepest integration of the principality into European structures since the 1991 customs union.

title: Foreign Property Purchase Restrictions
description: The Espot government tightened restrictions on foreign property acquisition and introduced higher transaction taxes on non-resident buyers in response to ongoing housing affordability protests. The measures represented a notable departure from Andorra's traditional openness to foreign capital.
